summary.vi: Adam dẫn Eve tới trung tâm Eden và chỉ cho nàng Cây Sự Sống, Cây Tri Thức cùng lời cấm không được ăn quả. Eve phân biệt điều Adam đã chứng kiến với điều chàng chỉ được truyền lại, trong khi Thư Khố xác nhận hồ sơ gốc không chứa phần giải thích. Ngoài Eden, Lilith tự kiểm nghiệm một loại quả và tạo dấu cho trạng thái “chưa biết”. Trước Cây Tri Thức, Eve tự đặt hai viên đá làm điểm dừng, hỏi lời cấm đang bảo vệ sự sống của nàng hay chính lời cấm. Thiên Đàng ghi câu hỏi nhưng không trả lời thay. Một chiếc lá rơi giữa hai viên đá; Adam và Eve không xem đó là đáp án.
summary.en: Adam leads Eve to Eden’s center and shows her the Tree of Life, the Tree of Knowledge, and the prohibition against eating its fruit. Eve distinguishes what Adam has witnessed from what he has only been told, while the Archive confirms that the original record contains no explanation. Beyond Eden, Lilith tests a wild fruit and creates a mark for the state of not yet knowing. Before the Tree of Knowledge, Eve sets two stones as her own stopping point and asks whether the prohibition protects her life or merely itself. Heaven records the question but does not answer in her place. A leaf falls between the stones; neither Adam nor Eve calls it an answer.

content_markdown_vi:
Adam dẫn Eve về phía trung tâm Eden khi sương còn nằm trên mặt lá.

Chàng không mang theo túi nước, dây hay dao đá.

Eve nhận ra điều đó trước khi họ đi hết hàng cây đầu tiên.

*“Không cần?”*

Adam nhìn hai bàn tay trống của mình.

*“Ở đây, nước ở gần. Đường bằng. Không có gai như ngoài ranh giới.”*

*“Gần không có nghĩa an toàn.”*

Đó là lời Adam đã nói với nàng ngày hôm trước. Khi nghe nó trở lại từ miệng Eve, chàng chậm bước.

*“Không,” chàng nói. “Không có nghĩa như vậy.”*

Họ đi qua nơi dòng nước tách thành ba nhánh. Một nhánh uốn về nơi trú. Một nhánh vòng quanh vườn quả. Nhánh còn lại chảy thẳng vào vùng cây mọc thưa hơn ở giữa Eden.

Eve chọn nhánh thứ ba.

Adam đi bên cạnh, không bước lên trước.

Ở những phần khác của khu vườn, sự sống chen vào nhau. Dây leo quấn quanh thân gỗ. Cỏ mọc sát mép nước. Chim nhỏ hạ xuống những cành thấp đến mức Eve chỉ cần đưa tay là có thể cảm thấy hơi ấm dưới lớp lông ngực.

Càng vào sâu, khoảng cách giữa các thân cây càng đều.

Không cành nào vượt sang khoảng của cây khác.

Không rễ nào trồi lên khỏi đất.

Mặt đất sạch đến mức giống một sân nghi lễ hơn là phần đất mọc tự nhiên giữa rừng.

Eve dừng lại.

*“Ai giữ nơi này?”*

*“Không ai.”*

Nàng cúi xuống. Một chiếc lá khô nằm giữa hai viên đá nhẵn. Những chiếc lá khác quanh đó vẫn xanh.

*“Vậy ai dọn?”*

Adam không trả lời ngay.

Chàng đã sống trong Eden đủ lâu để biết quả nào chín trước mưa, con vật nào tìm bóng vào buổi sáng và nhánh sông nào đổi dòng sau gió lớn.

Nhưng chàng chưa từng thấy ai dọn lá ở đây.

*“Ta không biết.”*

Eve ngẩng lên.

Đó không phải câu trả lời nàng chờ. Có lẽ vì nó là câu trả lời đầu tiên Adam không cố làm cho trọn vẹn.

Nàng đặt chiếc lá trở lại chỗ cũ.

*“Tốt.”*

*“Tốt?”*

*“Ngươi biết chỗ mình không biết.”*

Adam nhìn nàng một lúc rồi tiếp tục đi.

✦

Hai cây đứng ở cuối lối nước.

Chúng không cao nhất Eden. Không thân nào lớn đến mức phải ngửa đầu mới thấy tán. Nhưng mọi đường trong khu vườn dường như đều có thể dẫn đến đây, trừ khi người đi chủ ý tránh nó.

Cây bên trái mang lá dài, xanh thẫm. Trên mỗi lá có một đường sáng mảnh chạy từ cuống đến đầu, chậm như nhịp thở. Quả của nó trong gần như nước, chỉ hiện rõ khi ánh sáng đi xuyên qua và để lại một vòng nhạt giữa tán.

Cây bên phải thấp hơn. Vỏ thân xám, mang những đường nhỏ tách ra rồi gặp lại như nét viết chưa thành chữ. Quả mọc rải rác. Nhìn từ phía đông, chúng có màu đồng. Eve bước sang một bước, màu đồng chuyển thành đỏ sẫm.

Gió vẫn đi qua Eden.

Hai tán cây không chuyển động.

Eve nhìn Adam.

*“Nguy hiểm?”*

Adam chỉ cây bên phải.

*“Ta được phán không ăn quả của cây ấy.”*

*“Còn cây kia?”*

*“Không có lời cấm nào được trao cho ta về nó.”*

*“Vậy ngươi biết nó không nguy hiểm?”*

Adam nhìn những đường sáng chạy trên lá.

*“Không.”*

Eve bước vào khoảng giữa hai bóng cây.

*“Tên?”*

Adam đặt tay lên ngực, như thể câu trả lời nằm ở đó từ trước khi chàng học nói.

*“Cây Sự Sống.” Chàng chỉ sang trái. “Cây Tri Thức.”*

Eve lặp lại từng tên.

*“Sự sống.”*

Những đường sáng trên lá cây bên trái đi qua thêm một nhịp.

*“Tri thức.”*

Màu trên quả cây bên phải tối lại khi một đám mây mỏng đi qua ánh trời.

*“Ai đặt tên?”*

*“Tên đã có khi ta đến.”*

*“Ngươi nghe từ ai?”*

Adam nhìn lên khoảng sáng phía trên hai tán cây.

*“Từ Người.”*

Eve không hỏi Người là ai. Nàng đã cảm nhận sự hiện diện ấy trong lần đầu mở mắt, như sức nóng còn lại trên đá sau khi ánh sáng rời đi.

Nàng hỏi điều khác.

*“Cây Tri Thức làm gì?”*

*“Không được ăn quả.”*

*“Ta hỏi nó làm gì.”*

Adam khép miệng.

Bên ngoài Eden, nguy hiểm đã có hình dạng: gai, đất lún, bóng tối, vết cắt. Chàng có thể chỉ vào từng thứ và nói điều gì có thể xảy ra nếu Eve đặt chân sai.

Ở đây, chàng chỉ có một câu được trao trước khi có người thứ hai để hỏi lại.

*“Ta không biết.”*

Eve nhìn quả gần nhất.

*“Điều nguy hiểm là quả?”*

*“Lời phán nói không được ăn.”*

*“Vì sao?”*

*“Không nói.”*

*“Điều gì sẽ xảy ra?”*

*“Có nói.”*

*“Điều gì?”*

Adam nhìn nàng.

*“Cái chết.”*

Âm cuối rơi xuống khoảng đất sạch giữa họ.

Không con chim nào ngừng hót. Không dòng nước nào đổi nhịp.

Nhưng Eve đứng yên lâu hơn.

*“Cái chết là gì?”*

Adam nhớ những mảnh xương trắng ở xa Eden, nơi chàng và Lilith từng đi qua mà chưa biết tên của sự vắng mặt nằm trong chúng. Chàng nhớ một con vật nhỏ không thức dậy sau đêm lạnh. Nhớ Lilith đặt tay lên ngực nó rồi lắc đầu.

*“Là khi sự sống không trở lại.”*

*“Ngươi đã chết?”*

*“Chưa.”*

*“Ngươi biết từ người đã chết?”*

*“Không.”*

*“Vậy ngươi biết thế nào?”*

Adam không có câu trả lời khác.

*“Ta được nói.”*

Eve quay lại nhìn hai cây.

Một cây mang tên điều Adam biết qua chính cơ thể mình.

Cây còn lại mang tên điều chàng bị cấm đạt tới.

Giữa chúng là một hậu quả không ai trong hai người có thể trở về để kể lại.

Eve nhìn bàn chân đã lành dưới lớp vải buộc mỏng.

*“Ngày hôm qua, ngươi biết đá có thể cắt ta.”*

*“Có.”*

*“Vì ngươi đã thấy đá cắt.”*

*“Có.”*

*“Còn cái chết này, ngươi chưa thấy từ quả.”*

Adam không rời mắt khỏi nàng.

*“Ta vẫn tin lời phán.”*

*“Ta không hỏi ngươi có tin.”*

Eve chỉ vào khoảng đất giữa họ.

*“Ta hỏi điều nào ngươi biết bằng mắt, điều nào ngươi biết bằng lời.”*

Adam nhìn xuống.

Chàng nhặt hai viên đá nhỏ nằm gần dòng nước, đặt một viên trước chân Eve và một viên trước chân mình.

*“Cái này,” chàng nói, chạm viên trước nàng, “là điều ta đã thấy.”*

Chàng chạm viên còn lại.

*“Cái này là điều ta được trao.”*

*“Không giống nhau.”*

*“Không.”*

*“Nhưng cả hai đều có thể đúng.”*

Adam gật đầu chậm hơn.

*“Có.”*

Eve nhìn khoảng trống giữa hai viên đá.

*“Và phần này?”*

Adam không đặt thêm gì vào đó.

*“Điều ta chưa biết.”*

✦

Tại Thư Khố, bản ghi quan sát hiện lên theo quy trình đã được thiết lập từ trước.

Không chuông.

Không hình ảnh.

Chỉ một phiến chữ nổi lên trên bàn ghi.

**EVE: TIẾP CẬN VÙNG TRUNG TÂM EDEN.**

**ADAM: HIỆN DIỆN.**

**KHÔNG GHI NHẬN TIẾP XÚC VẬT CHẤT VỚI QUẢ.**

Gabriel đọc ba dòng rồi nhìn phiến đá thứ bảy.

Nó không sáng.

Michael đứng bên phải bàn ghi. Chàng không mặc giáp nghi lễ; chỉ có dây đeo kiếm và chiếc găng bạc ở tay trái. Bàn tay phải để trần, không mang dấu quyền nào đối với nhánh Nhân Loại.

“Hồ sơ lời cấm,” Gabriel nói.

Một dải chữ khác hiện ra theo lệnh truy xuất.

**QUY TẮC TRUNG TÂM: KHÔNG TIÊU THỤ QUẢ TỪ CÂY TRI THỨC.**

**HỆ QUẢ ĐÃ GHI: TỬ VONG.**

**NGUỒN: LỜI PHÁN NGUYÊN THỦY.**

Healiangel bước đến gần hơn.

*“Có phần giải thích không?”*

Gabriel đưa đầu trượng qua dải chữ.

Không có lớp văn bản nào mở phía sau.

Ngài thử lại bằng dấu truy nguyên.

Bề mặt bàn ghi chỉ phản chiếu khuôn mặt của ba người.

*“Không.”*

“Bị niêm?” Michael hỏi.

*“Không có chỉ dấu niêm.”*

*“Bị xóa?”*

*“Không có dấu khuyết.”*

Healiangel đặt tay dưới phần cánh trái đã mất.

*“Vậy bản ghi được tạo mà không có phần ấy.”*

Gabriel nhìn anh.

*“Lời phán không cần biện minh để có hiệu lực.”*

*“Hiệu lực đối với ai?”*

*“Đối với Nhân Loại.”*

*“Ta hỏi ai xác nhận nó đã được hiểu.”*

Gabriel hạ trượng.

*“Adam đã tiếp nhận.”*

“Tiếp nhận không phải hiểu,” Michael nói.

*“Ngươi đang phân biệt điều trước đây Thiên Đàng chưa từng phân biệt.”*

*“Vì trước đây chúng ta chưa từng được giao dẫn dắt một sinh linh có thể hỏi lại.”*

Một ánh vàng chạm vòng niêm ngoài cùng.

Lucifer dừng ở phía bên kia.

Y không bước qua.

*“Tử vong,” y đọc. “Một hậu quả không hình ảnh. Một mệnh lệnh không nguyên nhân được ghi.”*

Gabriel xoay trượng về phía y.

*“Ngươi không có quyền diễn giải hồ sơ Nhân Loại.”*

*“Ta đang đọc điều hồ sơ chứa.”*

*“Và chuẩn bị đặt phần ngươi muốn vào chỗ trống.”*

Lucifer nhìn Healiangel.

*“Chỗ trống đã ở đó trước khi ta đến.”*

Khoảng thiếu dưới cánh Healiangel siết lại.

Không đau.

Chỉ là một chuyển động rất nhỏ, như vết thương đã khép nhận ra thời tiết đổi bên ngoài bức tường.

“Đừng chạm vào nàng,” anh nói.

Lucifer không mỉm cười.

*“Ta chưa chạm.”*

*“Đừng trả lời thay chỉ vì Thiên Đàng chưa có câu trả lời.”*

*“Vậy các ngươi nên nói rõ điều mình biết trước khi kẻ khác biến phần im lặng thành chân lý của hắn.”*

Michael quay sang y.

*“Đó là đe dọa?”*

*“Là cảnh báo.”*

*“Cảnh báo phải dừng trước quyền quyết định.”*

Lucifer nhìn bàn tay trần của Michael.

*“Ta thấy ngươi đã học câu ấy.”*

Y lùi khỏi vòng niêm một bước.

Không ai yêu cầu.

Chính điều đó khiến Healiangel nhìn theo lâu hơn.

✦

Ngoài ba dãy đá, Lilith đập một quả dại bằng mặt phẳng con dao.

Quả không mở.

Nàng đổi góc, đặt nó vào hõm đá rồi dùng chuôi dao gõ lần nữa. Vỏ nứt thành ba đường. Mùi chua bốc lên, làm mắt nàng cay.

Con vật mẹ bên bờ suối ngẩng đầu.

Lilith đưa phần thịt quả lên mũi, không ăn.

Nàng chạm một ít vào mặt trong cổ tay.

Chờ.

Không bỏng. Không ngứa.

Nàng đặt một mẩu nhỏ lên đầu lưỡi rồi nhổ ra ngay. Vị chua mạnh đến mức nước mắt dâng lên, nhưng không làm tê miệng.

Con vật mẹ nhìn nàng rồi nhìn quả.

“Không biết,” Lilith nói.

Nó không tiến lại.

Nàng cắt phần thịt thành hai mẩu, đặt một mẩu cạnh tổ côn trùng dưới gốc cây và giữ mẩu còn lại trên phiến đá.

Những sinh vật nhỏ đến trước. Chúng chạm râu, cắn một phần, lùi lại rồi trở về.

Lilith đợi cho đến khi mặt trời đi được một khoảng trên sườn đá.

Không con nào chết.

Nàng ăn một miếng nhỏ.

Vị chua vẫn khó chịu. Phía sau nó có vị ngọt mỏng, chỉ hiện ra khi nàng giữ đủ lâu trong miệng.

Lilith nhìn phần quả còn lại.

Không lời phán nào nói nàng được ăn.

Không lời phán nào nói nàng không được.

Cơ thể, thời gian và hậu quả chỉ trả lời từng phần.

Nàng khắc lên phiến đá một đường cong mở ở đầu.

Chưa an toàn.

Chưa nguy hiểm.

Chưa biết.

Nàng đặt phiến đá cạnh cửa nơi trú.

Ở nơi nằm ngoài phạm vi quan sát chi tiết của Eden, một con người vừa tạo dấu cho điều Thiên Đàng chưa có ô để ghi.

✦

Eve bước đến gần Cây Tri Thức.

Adam không giữ nàng lại.

Nhưng cơ thể chàng làm điều lời nói đã dừng: vai căng, bàn chân xoay về phía trước, bàn tay phải mở ra rồi khép lại.

Eve thấy.

*“Ngươi muốn ngăn.”*

*“Có.”*

*“Vì lời phán?”*

*“Vì ta không muốn ngươi chết.”*

*“Hai điều giống nhau?”*

Adam nhìn quả thấp nhất rồi nhìn nàng.

*“Ta không biết.”*

Eve đi thêm một bước.

Bóng cây phủ qua bàn chân nàng. Không lạnh. Không nóng. Không khác bóng của bất kỳ thân cây nào khác trong Eden.

Nàng đưa tay lên.

Adam hít vào.

Eve dừng khi ngón tay còn cách quả một khoảng bằng chiều rộng móng tay.

*“Ta chưa chạm.”*

*“Ta thấy.”*

*“Nguy hiểm bắt đầu ở đâu?”*

*“Khi ăn.”*

*“Chạm?”*

*“Lời phán không nói.”*

*“Hái?”*

*“Không nói.”*

*“Ngửi?”*

*“Không nói.”*

*“Hỏi?”*

Adam im lặng.

Eve hạ tay.

Nàng đi quanh thân cây. Vỏ xám mang những đường tách rồi gặp lại, nhưng không đường nào hoàn thành một hình. Ở phía sau, rễ nổi lên một đoạn ngắn trước khi chìm xuống đất. Giữa hai rễ có một hòn đá đen, nhỏ hơn viên Lilith từng để lại nhưng cùng màu.

Eve không nhặt viên đá ấy.

Nàng tìm hai viên đá sáng ở mép nước, đặt chúng tại rìa bóng cây, cách nhau một bàn tay.

“Dấu gì?” Adam hỏi.

*“Nơi ta dừng.”*

*“Vì lời cấm?”*

*“Vì ta chưa biết.”*

Adam nhìn hai viên đá.

*“Khác nhau?”*

*“Có.”*

Eve chỉ viên gần Adam.

*“Nếu ta chỉ dừng vì ngươi sợ, bước chân này sẽ luôn phải chờ nỗi sợ của ngươi.”*

Nàng chỉ viên còn lại.

*“Nếu ta bước vì muốn chống lại lời phán, bước chân cũng không còn thuộc về điều ta thấy.”*

Nàng đặt bàn tay lên khoảng đất giữa hai viên.

*“Ta dừng ở đây vì phần này chưa có câu trả lời.”*

Adam nhìn bàn tay mình.

Ngày trước, chàng đã đặt đá để chỉ đường cho Lilith trở lại.

Bây giờ Eve đặt đá để ghi nơi nàng tự chọn chưa bước qua.

*“Ta có thể ở cùng?”*

Eve nhìn khoảng trống bên cạnh.

*“Có.”*

Adam ngồi xuống.

Không chắn giữa nàng và cây.

Không đứng sau lưng nàng.

Chàng ngồi cùng phía với câu hỏi.

Một lúc lâu, chỉ có tiếng nước phía sau họ.

Eve nhìn quả gần nhất.

*“Khi ta chưa biết,” nàng nói, “điều được bảo vệ là sự sống của ta, hay chỉ là lời cấm?”*

Adam không vội đáp.

*“Ta muốn là sự sống của ngươi.”*

*“Ngươi muốn không phải câu trả lời.”*

*“Không.”*

*“Vậy ai biết?”*

Adam nhìn lên khoảng sáng không có hình dạng phía trên hai tán cây.

*“Người đã phán.”*

Eve chờ.

Không giọng nói nào đi qua lá.

✦

Trong Thư Khố, một dòng mới được tạo dưới hồ sơ quan sát.

Không phải cảnh báo.

Không phải vi phạm.

Không phải yêu cầu phê chuẩn.

**EVE: TIẾP CẬN GIỚI HẠN ĐÃ CÔNG BỐ.**

**EVE: KHÔNG TIẾP XÚC QUẢ.**

**EVE: TỰ THIẾT LẬP ĐIỂM DỪNG.**

Gabriel đọc dòng cuối hai lần.

*“Hệ thống không có phân loại tương ứng.”*

“Vậy giữ nguyên mô tả,” Michael nói.

*“Mọi hành vi quanh vùng trung tâm đều phải có trạng thái.”*

*“Đã có trạng thái.”*

*“Tên của trạng thái?”*

Healiangel nhìn phiến chữ.

Đường cong trong khoảng thiếu dưới cánh anh ngừng dịch chuyển.

Không biến mất.

Chỉ dừng ở một hình dạng chưa khép.

“Chưa quyết định,” anh nói.

Gabriel nhìn anh.

*“Đó không phải trạng thái Thiên Đàng cho phép duy trì.”*

*“Nhưng đó là điều đã xảy ra.”*

Gabriel chưa đáp thì một phiến ghi phụ sáng lên theo đường truyền quan sát.

Ký tự hiện ra chậm, không hoàn toàn theo cú pháp của Thiên Đàng.

**KHI TA CHƯA BIẾT, ĐIỀU ĐƯỢC BẢO VỆ LÀ SỰ SỐNG CỦA TA, HAY LỜI CẤM?**

Gabriel đưa trượng lên.

Michael giữ cổ tay ngài lại.

Không mạnh.

Chỉ đủ để đầu trượng dừng trước mặt chữ.

*“Không xóa.”*

*“Nó không phải lời phán.”*

*“Không ai nói nó là lời phán.”*

*“Nó không thuộc cấu trúc hồ sơ.”*

*“Bây giờ thuộc phần quan sát.”*

*“Ai đã ghi?”*

Healiangel nhìn xuống Eden.

Eve vẫn ngồi cạnh Adam ở mép bóng cây. Môi nàng đã khép. Không có đường hồi đáp từ Thư Khố xuống nàng.

*“Câu hỏi của nàng được ghi lại,” anh nói. “Không hơn.”*

Gabriel nhìn mặt chữ.

*“Hệ thống không có câu trả lời.”*

Michael buông cổ tay ngài.

*“Ghi điều đã xảy ra.”*

Không ai thêm lời giải thích.

Không ai biến câu hỏi thành vi phạm.

Không ai trả lời thay.

Ở trung tâm Eden, hai tán cây vẫn đứng im.

Một chiếc lá rời khỏi Cây Tri Thức.

Không gió chạm vào tán.

Không ánh sáng đổi nhịp.

Không ai biết vì sao cuống lá buông ra đúng lúc ấy.

Chiếc lá xoay một vòng rồi đáp xuống khoảng đất giữa hai viên đá Eve đã đặt — ngay trên nơi nàng tự chọn dừng lại.

Eve nhìn nó.

Adam cũng nhìn.

Không ai gọi đó là câu trả lời.

Adam led Eve toward Eden’s center while dew still lay upon the leaves.

He carried no water skin, cord, or stone knife.

Eve noticed before they had passed the first row of trees.

*“We will not need them?”*

Adam looked at his empty hands.

*“Here, water is near. The ground is level. There are no thorns like those beyond the boundary.”*

*“Close does not mean safe.”*

Those were words Adam had spoken to her the day before. Hearing them return from Eve’s mouth slowed his step.

*“No,” he said. “That is not what it means.”*

They passed the place where the water divided into three branches. One curved toward the shelter. One circled the orchard. The last ran straight into the more sparsely wooded ground at Eden’s center.

Eve chose the third branch.

Adam walked beside her and did not move ahead.

Elsewhere in the garden, life pressed into life. Vines wound around trunks. Grass crowded the water’s edge. Small birds settled upon branches low enough that Eve need only reach out to feel the warmth beneath their breast feathers.

The deeper they went, the more even the spaces between the trunks became.

No branch crossed into another tree’s reach.

No root broke the surface of the earth.

The ground was so clean it resembled a ritual court more than earth grown naturally within a forest.

Eve stopped.

*“Who tends this place?”*

*“No one.”*

She bent down. A dry leaf lay between two smooth stones. The other leaves around it remained green.

*“Then who clears it?”*

Adam did not answer at once.

He had lived in Eden long enough to know which fruit ripened before rain, which animals sought shade in the morning, and which branch of the river changed course after a hard wind.

But he had never seen anyone clear the leaves here.

*“I do not know.”*

Eve looked up.

It was not the answer she had expected. Perhaps because it was the first answer Adam had not tried to make complete.

She set the leaf back where it had been.

*“Good.”*

*“Good?”*

*“You know where your knowing ends.”*

Adam regarded her for a moment, then walked on.

✦

The two trees stood at the end of the waterway.

They were not the tallest in Eden. Neither trunk was so vast that one had to throw back the head to see its crown. Yet every path in the garden seemed capable of leading here, unless the traveler deliberately turned away.

The tree on the left bore long, deep-green leaves. A fine line of light ran from stem to tip along each one, slow as breath. Its fruit was almost as clear as water, visible only when light passed through it and left a pale ring suspended among the branches.

The tree on the right stood lower. Its bark was gray, marked by narrow lines that parted and met again like strokes of writing not yet formed into words. Fruit grew sparsely across its limbs. Seen from the east, it was bronze. Eve moved one step aside, and the bronze deepened into dark red.

Wind still moved through Eden.

The crowns of the two trees did not stir.

Eve looked at Adam.

*“Danger?”*

Adam pointed to the tree on the right.

*“I was commanded not to eat the fruit of that tree.”*

*“And the other?”*

*“No prohibition was given to me concerning the other.”*

*“Then do you know it is not dangerous?”*

Adam watched the lines of light moving through the leaves.

*“No.”*

Eve stepped into the space between the two shadows.

*“Their names?”*

Adam placed a hand upon his chest, as though the answer had been there before he learned to speak.

*“The Tree of Life.” He pointed left. “The Tree of Knowledge.”*

Eve repeated each name.

*“Life.”*

The lines of light upon the leaves of the left-hand tree passed through another pulse.

*“Knowledge.”*

The fruit of the right-hand tree darkened as a thin cloud crossed the light above.

*“Who named them?”*

*“Their names were here when I came.”*

*“From whom did you hear them?”*

Adam looked toward the brightness above the two crowns.

*“From Him.”*

Eve did not ask who He was. She had felt that presence when she first opened her eyes, like heat lingering upon stone after the light had moved away.

She asked something else.

*“What does the Tree of Knowledge do?”*

*“Its fruit must not be eaten.”*

*“I asked what it does.”*

Adam closed his mouth.

Beyond Eden, danger had possessed a shape: thorn, sinking earth, darkness, a cut in the flesh. He could point to each and tell Eve what might happen if she placed her foot wrongly.

Here, he had only a sentence given before there was a second person to question it.

*“I do not know.”*

Eve looked at the nearest fruit.

*“Is the fruit what is dangerous?”*

*“The Decree says it must not be eaten.”*

*“Why?”*

*“It does not say.”*

*“What will happen?”*

*“It does say.”*

*“What?”*

Adam looked at her.

*“Death.”*

The final sound fell into the clean earth between them.

No bird ceased its song. No stream altered its rhythm.

But Eve stood still for longer.

*“What is death?”*

Adam remembered the white fragments of bone far beyond Eden, where he and Lilith had once walked without knowing the name of the absence held within them. He remembered a small animal that had not awakened after a cold night. He remembered Lilith pressing her hand to its chest, then shaking her head.

*“It is when life does not return.”*

*“Have you died?”*

*“No.”*

*“Do you know it from someone who has?”*

*“No.”*

*“Then how do you know?”*

Adam had no other answer.

*“I was told.”*

Eve turned back toward the trees.

One tree bore the name of what Adam knew through his own body.

The other bore the name of what he had been forbidden to attain.

Between them lay a consequence neither of them could return from to describe.

Eve looked at the healed foot beneath its thin binding.

*“Yesterday, you knew stone could cut me.”*

*“Yes.”*

*“Because you had seen stone cut.”*

*“Yes.”*

*“But this death—you have not seen it come from the fruit.”*

Adam did not look away from her.

*“I still believe the Decree.”*

*“I did not ask whether you believe.”*

Eve pointed to the ground between them.

*“I asked which part you know by sight, and which part you know by word.”*

Adam looked down.

He picked up two small stones beside the water and set one before Eve’s feet and the other before his own.

*“This,” he said, touching the stone before her, “is what I have seen.”*

He touched the other stone.

*“This is what was given to me.”*

*“They are not the same.”*

*“No.”*

*“But both may be true.”*

Adam nodded more slowly.

*“Yes.”*

Eve looked at the empty space between the two stones.

*“And this part?”*

Adam placed nothing more within it.

*“What I do not know.”*

✦

Within the Archive, the observation record appeared through the process established beforehand.

No bell sounded.

No image appeared.

Only a tablet of script rose above the recording table.

**EVE: ENTERED THE CENTRAL REGION OF EDEN.**

**ADAM: PRESENT.**

**NO PHYSICAL CONTACT WITH THE FRUIT RECORDED.**

Gabriel read the three lines, then looked toward the seventh tablet.

It did not kindle.

Michael stood to the right of the recording table. He wore no ceremonial armor, only his sword-belt and a silver glove upon his left hand. His right hand was bare, bearing no mark of authority over the branch of Humanity.

“The prohibition record,” Gabriel said.

Another band of script appeared at the retrieval command.

**CENTRAL LAW: DO NOT CONSUME FRUIT FROM THE TREE OF KNOWLEDGE.**

**RECORDED CONSEQUENCE: DEATH.**

**SOURCE: THE ORIGINAL DECREE.**

Healiangel stepped closer.

*“Is there an explanation?”*

Gabriel passed the head of his staff across the inscription.

No further layer of text opened behind it.

He tried again with the sign of provenance.

The surface of the recording table reflected only the faces of the three.

*“No.”*

“Sealed?” Michael asked.

*“There is no seal-marker.”*

*“Erased?”*

*“There is no mark of omission.”*

Healiangel placed a hand beneath the missing part of his left wing.

*“Then the record was created without that part.”*

Gabriel looked at him.

*“A Decree requires no justification to remain in force.”*

*“Binding upon whom?”*

*“Upon Humanity.”*

*“I asked who confirmed that it was understood.”*

Gabriel lowered his staff.

*“Adam received it.”*

“Receiving is not understanding,” Michael said.

*“You distinguish what Heaven has never before distinguished.”*

*“Because Heaven has never before been charged with guiding a being that can question what it is told.”*

A touch of gold reached the outermost sealed ring.

Lucifer stopped on the far side.

He did not cross it.

*“Death,” he read. “A consequence without image. A command with no cause recorded.”*

Gabriel turned his staff toward him.

*“You have no authority to interpret the record of Humanity.”*

*“I am reading what the record contains.”*

*“And preparing to place what you desire inside the empty space.”*

Lucifer looked at Healiangel.

*“The empty space was there before I arrived.”*

The hollow beneath Healiangel’s wing tightened.

Not pain.

Only the smallest movement, like a wound long closed realizing that the weather beyond the wall had changed.

“Do not touch her,” he said.

Lucifer did not smile.

*“I have not.”*

*“Do not answer in another’s place merely because Heaven has no answer.”*

*“Then you should state clearly what you know before someone else turns the silence into his own truth.”*

Michael turned to him.

*“Is that a threat?”*

*“A warning.”*

*“A warning must end before the right to choose begins.”*

Lucifer looked at Michael’s bare hand.

*“I see you have learned that sentence.”*

He stepped back from the sealed ring.

No one had ordered him to.

That was why Healiangel watched him longer.

✦

Beyond the three ridges of stone, Lilith struck a wild fruit with the flat of her knife.

It did not split.

She changed the angle, set it in a hollow of rock, and struck again with the pommel. The rind cracked in three lines. A sour scent rose and stung her eyes.

The mother animal by the stream lifted its head.

Lilith raised the flesh of the fruit to her nose, but did not eat.

She rubbed a little against the inside of her wrist.

Waited.

No burning. No itch.

She placed a small piece upon the tip of her tongue and spat it out at once. The sourness was strong enough to bring tears to her eyes, but it did not numb her mouth.

The mother animal looked at her, then at the fruit.

“I do not know,” Lilith said.

It did not come closer.

She cut the flesh into two pieces, placed one beside an insect nest beneath the tree, and kept the other upon the stone slab.

The small creatures came first. They touched it with their feelers, bit away a piece, withdrew, then returned.

Lilith waited until the sun had moved some distance along the face of the rocks.

None of them died.

She ate a small piece.

The sourness remained unpleasant. Behind it lay a thin sweetness that appeared only when she kept the fruit in her mouth long enough.

Lilith looked at what remained of the fruit.

No Decree had said she might eat it.

No Decree had said she might not.

Body, time, and consequence answered only in parts.

She carved an open-ended curve into the stone slab.

Not safe.

Not dangerous.

Not yet known.

She placed the slab beside the entrance to her shelter.

Beyond the range of Eden’s detailed observation, a human being had made a sign for something Heaven possessed no field in which to record.

✦

Eve stepped closer to the Tree of Knowledge.

Adam did not restrain her.

But his body did what his words had ceased to do: his shoulders tightened, one foot turned forward, and his right hand opened, then closed.

Eve saw.

*“You want to stop me.”*

*“Yes.”*

*“Because of the Decree?”*

*“Because I do not want you to die.”*

*“Are those the same?”*

Adam looked at the lowest fruit, then at her.

*“I do not know.”*

Eve took one more step.

The tree’s shadow passed over her feet. Not cold. Not warm. No different from the shade of any other tree in Eden.

She raised her hand.

Adam drew breath.

Eve stopped with the width of a fingernail between her fingers and the fruit.

*“I have not touched it.”*

*“I see.”*

*“Where does the danger begin?”*

*“When it is eaten.”*

*“Touching it?”*

*“The Decree does not say.”*

*“Plucked?”*

*“It does not say.”*

*“Smelled?”*

*“It does not say.”*

*“Questioned?”*

Adam remained silent.

Eve lowered her hand.

She walked around the trunk. The gray bark bore lines that divided and met again, but none completed a shape. Behind the tree, one root rose briefly above the earth before sinking back beneath it. Between two roots lay a black stone, smaller than the one Lilith had once left behind, but the same color.

Eve did not pick up that stone.

She found two pale stones at the water’s edge and set them at the border of the tree’s shadow, one handspan apart.

“What is the mark?” Adam asked.

*“Where I stop.”*

*“Because of the prohibition?”*

*“Because I do not yet know.”*

Adam looked at the two stones.

*“Is there a difference?”*

*“Yes.”*

Eve pointed to the stone nearer Adam.

*“If I stop only because you are afraid, this step will always have to wait upon your fear.”*

She pointed to the other stone.

*“If I step forward merely to defy the Decree, the step will no longer belong to what I see.”*

She placed her hand upon the ground between the two stones.

*“I stop here because this part has no answer yet.”*

Adam looked at his hands.

Long ago, he had set stones to show Lilith the way back.

Now Eve set stones to mark the place she had chosen not to cross.

*“May I remain with you?”*

Eve looked at the open space beside her.

*“Yes.”*

Adam sat down.

He did not place himself between her and the tree.

He did not stand behind her.

He sat on the same side as the question.

For a long while, there was only the sound of water behind them.

Eve looked at the nearest fruit.

*“When I do not know,” she said, “what is being protected—my life, or only the prohibition?”*

Adam did not answer in haste.

*“I want it to be your life.”*

*“What you want is not an answer.”*

*“No.”*

*“Then who knows?”*

Adam looked toward the shapeless brightness above the two crowns.

*“He who gave the Decree.”*

Eve waited.

No voice passed through the leaves.

✦

Within the Archive, a new line was created beneath the observation record.

Not a warning.

Not a violation.

Not a request for sanction.

**EVE: APPROACHED THE DECLARED LIMIT.**

**EVE: MADE NO CONTACT WITH THE FRUIT.**

**EVE: ESTABLISHED HER OWN STOPPING POINT.**

Gabriel read the final line twice.

*“The system has no corresponding classification.”*

“Then preserve the description as it stands,” Michael said.

*“Every act near the central region must bear a status.”*

*“It already has a status.”*

*“What is the status called?”*

Healiangel looked at the tablet.

The curve within the hollow beneath his wing ceased to move.

It did not disappear.

It merely stopped in an unfinished shape.

“Undecided,” he said.

Gabriel looked at him.

*“That is not a state Heaven permits to endure.”*

*“But it is what occurred.”*

Before Gabriel could answer, a secondary tablet lit along the observation channel.

The characters appeared slowly, not wholly following the syntax of Heaven.

**WHEN I DO NOT KNOW, WHAT IS BEING PROTECTED—MY LIFE, OR THE PROHIBITION?**

Gabriel raised his staff.

Michael caught his wrist.

Not forcefully.

Only enough to halt the staff before it reached the words.

*“Do not erase it.”*

*“It is not a Decree.”*

*“No one said it was.”*

*“It does not belong to the structure of the record.”*

*“It now belongs to the observation.”*

*“Who inscribed it?”*

Healiangel looked down toward Eden.

Eve still sat beside Adam at the edge of the tree’s shadow. Her lips had closed. No path of reply ran from the Archive down to her.

*“Her question was recorded,” he said. “Nothing more.”*

Gabriel looked at the words.

*“The system has no answer.”*

Michael released his wrist.

*“Record what occurred.”*

No one added an explanation.

No one turned the question into a violation.

No one answered in her place.

At the heart of Eden, the two crowns remained still.

A leaf came free from the Tree of Knowledge.

No wind touched the crown.

No light altered its rhythm.

No one knew why the stem released at that moment.

The leaf turned once and came to rest upon the earth between the two stones Eve had placed—exactly where she had chosen to stop.

Eve looked at it.

Adam looked as well.

Neither of them called it an answer.

Chiếc lá xoay một vòng rồi đáp xuống khoảng đất giữa hai viên đá Eve đã đặt — ngay trên nơi nàng tự chọn dừng lại.

Eve nhìn nó.

Adam cũng nhìn.

Không ai gọi đó là câu trả lời.

Adam led Eve toward Eden’s center while dew still lay upon the leaves.

He carried no water skin, cord, or stone knife.

Eve noticed before they had passed the first row of trees.

“We will not need them?”

Adam looked at his empty hands.

“Here, water is near. The ground is level. There are no thorns like those beyond the boundary.”

“Close does not mean safe.”

Those were words Adam had spoken to her the day before. Hearing them return from Eve’s mouth slowed his step.

“No.” “That is not what it means.”

They passed the place where the water divided into three branches. One curved toward the shelter. One circled the orchard. The last ran straight into the more sparsely wooded ground at Eden’s center.

Eve chose the third branch.

Adam walked beside her and did not move ahead.

Elsewhere in the garden, life pressed into life. Vines wound around trunks. Grass crowded the water’s edge. Small birds settled upon branches low enough that Eve need only reach out to feel the warmth beneath their breast feathers.

The deeper they went, the more even the spaces between the trunks became.

No branch crossed into another tree’s reach.

No root broke the surface of the earth.

The ground was so clean it resembled a ritual court more than earth grown naturally within a forest.

Eve stopped.

“Who tends this place?”

“No one.”

She bent down. A dry leaf lay between two smooth stones. The other leaves around it remained green.

“Then who clears it?”

Adam did not answer at once.

He had lived in Eden long enough to know which fruit ripened before rain, which animals sought shade in the morning, and which branch of the river changed course after a hard wind.

But he had never seen anyone clear the leaves here.

“I do not know.”

Eve looked up.

It was not the answer she had expected. Perhaps because it was the first answer Adam had not tried to make complete.

She set the leaf back where it had been.

“Good.”

“Good?”

“You know where your knowing ends.”

Adam regarded her for a moment, then walked on.

✦

The two trees stood at the end of the waterway.

They were not the tallest in Eden. Neither trunk was so vast that one had to throw back the head to see its crown. Yet every path in the garden seemed capable of leading here, unless the traveler deliberately turned away.

The tree on the left bore long, deep-green leaves. A fine line of light ran from stem to tip along each one, slow as breath. Its fruit was almost as clear as water, visible only when light passed through it and left a pale ring suspended among the branches.

The tree on the right stood lower. Its bark was gray, marked by narrow lines that parted and met again like strokes of writing not yet formed into words. Fruit grew sparsely across its limbs. Seen from the east, it was bronze. Eve moved one step aside, and the bronze deepened into dark red.

Wind still moved through Eden.

The crowns of the two trees did not stir.

Eve looked at Adam.

“Danger?”

Adam pointed to the tree on the right.

“I was commanded not to eat the fruit of that tree.”

“And the other?”

“No prohibition was given to me concerning the other.”

“Then do you know it is not dangerous?”

Adam watched the lines of light moving through the leaves.

“No.”

Eve stepped into the space between the two shadows.

“Their names?”

Adam placed a hand upon his chest, as though the answer had been there before he learned to speak.

“The Tree of Life.” He pointed left. “The Tree of Knowledge.”

Eve repeated each name.

“Life.”

The lines of light upon the leaves of the left-hand tree passed through another pulse.

“Knowledge.”

The fruit of the right-hand tree darkened as a thin cloud crossed the light above.

“Who named them?”

“Their names were here when I came.”

“From whom did you hear them?”

Adam looked toward the brightness above the two crowns.

“From Him.”

Eve did not ask who He was. She had felt that presence when she first opened her eyes, like heat lingering upon stone after the light had moved away.

She asked something else.

“What does the Tree of Knowledge do?”

“Its fruit must not be eaten.”

“I asked what it does.”

Adam closed his mouth.

Beyond Eden, danger had possessed a shape: thorn, sinking earth, darkness, a cut in the flesh. He could point to each and tell Eve what might happen if she placed her foot wrongly.

Here, he had only a sentence given before there was a second person to question it.

“I do not know.”

Eve looked at the nearest fruit.

“Is the fruit what is dangerous?”

“The Decree says it must not be eaten.”

“Why?”

“It does not say.”

“What will happen?”

“It does say.”

“What?”

Adam looked at her.

“Death.”

The final sound fell into the clean earth between them.

No bird ceased its song. No stream altered its rhythm.

But Eve stood still for longer.

“What is death?”

Adam remembered the white fragments of bone far beyond Eden, where he and Lilith had once walked without knowing the name of the absence held within them. He remembered a small animal that had not awakened after a cold night. He remembered Lilith pressing her hand to its chest, then shaking her head.

“It is when life does not return.”

“Have you died?”

“No.”

“Do you know it from someone who has?”

“No.”

“Then how do you know?”

Adam had no other answer.

“I was told.”

Eve turned back toward the trees.

One tree bore the name of what Adam knew through his own body.

The other bore the name of what he had been forbidden to attain.

Between them lay a consequence neither of them could return from to describe.

Eve looked at the healed foot beneath its thin binding.

“Yesterday, you knew stone could cut me.”

“Yes.”

“Because you had seen stone cut.”

“Yes.”

“But this death—you have not seen it come from the fruit.”

Adam did not look away from her.

“I still believe the Decree.”

“I did not ask whether you believe.”

Eve pointed to the ground between them.

“I asked which part you know by sight, and which part you know by word.”

Adam looked down.

He picked up two small stones beside the water and set one before Eve’s feet and the other before his own.

“This,” he said, touching the stone before her, “is what I have seen.”

He touched the other stone.

“This is what was given to me.”

“They are not the same.”

“No.”

“But both may be true.”

Adam nodded more slowly.

“Yes.”

Eve looked at the empty space between the two stones.

“And this part?”

Adam placed nothing more within it.

“What I do not know.”

✦

Within the Archive, the observation record appeared through the process established beforehand.

No bell sounded.

No image appeared.

Only a tablet of script rose above the recording table.

EVE: ENTERED THE CENTRAL REGION OF EDEN.

ADAM: PRESENT.

NO PHYSICAL CONTACT WITH THE FRUIT RECORDED.

Gabriel read the three lines, then looked toward the seventh tablet.

It did not kindle.

Michael stood to the right of the recording table. He wore no ceremonial armor, only his sword-belt and a silver glove upon his left hand. His right hand was bare, bearing no mark of authority over the branch of Humanity.

“The prohibition record.”

Another band of script appeared at the retrieval command.

CENTRAL LAW: DO NOT CONSUME FRUIT FROM THE TREE OF KNOWLEDGE.

RECORDED CONSEQUENCE: DEATH.

SOURCE: THE ORIGINAL DECREE.

Healiangel stepped closer.

“Is there an explanation?”

Gabriel passed the head of his staff across the inscription.

No further layer of text opened behind it.

He tried again with the sign of provenance.

The surface of the recording table reflected only the faces of the three.

“No.”

“Sealed?”

“There is no seal-marker.”

“Erased?”

“There is no mark of omission.”

Healiangel placed a hand beneath the missing part of his left wing.

“Then the record was created without that part.”

Gabriel looked at him.

“A Decree requires no justification to remain in force.”

“Binding upon whom?”

“Upon Humanity.”

“I asked who confirmed that it was understood.”

Gabriel lowered his staff.

“Adam received it.”

“Receiving is not understanding.”

“You distinguish what Heaven has never before distinguished.”

“Because Heaven has never before been charged with guiding a being that can question what it is told.”

A touch of gold reached the outermost sealed ring.

Lucifer stopped on the far side.

He did not cross it.

“Death,” he read. “A consequence without image. A command with no cause recorded.”

Gabriel turned his staff toward him.

“You have no authority to interpret the record of Humanity.”

“I am reading what the record contains.”

“And preparing to place what you desire inside the empty space.”

Lucifer looked at Healiangel.

“The empty space was there before I arrived.”

The hollow beneath Healiangel’s wing tightened.

Not pain.

Only the smallest movement, like a wound long closed realizing that the weather beyond the wall had changed.

“Do not touch her.”

Lucifer did not smile.

“I have not.”

“Do not answer in another’s place merely because Heaven has no answer.”

“Then you should state clearly what you know before someone else turns the silence into his own truth.”

Michael turned to him.

“Is that a threat?”

“A warning.”

“A warning must end before the right to choose begins.”

Lucifer looked at Michael’s bare hand.

“I see you have learned that sentence.”

He stepped back from the sealed ring.

No one had ordered him to.

That was why Healiangel watched him longer.

✦

Beyond the three ridges of stone, Lilith struck a wild fruit with the flat of her knife.

It did not split.

She changed the angle, set it in a hollow of rock, and struck again with the pommel. The rind cracked in three lines. A sour scent rose and stung her eyes.

The mother animal by the stream lifted its head.

Lilith raised the flesh of the fruit to her nose, but did not eat.

She rubbed a little against the inside of her wrist.

Waited.

No burning. No itch.

She placed a small piece upon the tip of her tongue and spat it out at once. The sourness was strong enough to bring tears to her eyes, but it did not numb her mouth.

The mother animal looked at her, then at the fruit.

“I do not know,” Lilith said.

It did not come closer.

She cut the flesh into two pieces, placed one beside an insect nest beneath the tree, and kept the other upon the stone slab.

The small creatures came first. They touched it with their feelers, bit away a piece, withdrew, then returned.

Lilith waited until the sun had moved some distance along the face of the rocks.

None of them died.

She ate a small piece.

The sourness remained unpleasant. Behind it lay a thin sweetness that appeared only when she kept the fruit in her mouth long enough.

Lilith looked at what remained of the fruit.

No Decree had said she might eat it.

No Decree had said she might not.

Body, time, and consequence answered only in parts.

She carved an open-ended curve into the stone slab.

Not safe.

Not dangerous.

Not yet known.

She placed the slab beside the entrance to her shelter.

Beyond the range of Eden’s detailed observation, a human being had made a sign for something Heaven possessed no field in which to record.

✦

Eve stepped closer to the Tree of Knowledge.

Adam did not restrain her.

But his body did what his words had ceased to do: his shoulders tightened, one foot turned forward, and his right hand opened, then closed.

Eve saw.

“You want to stop me.”

“Yes.”

“Because of the Decree?”

“Because I do not want you to die.”

“Are those the same?”

Adam looked at the lowest fruit, then at her.

“I do not know.”

Eve took one more step.

The tree’s shadow passed over her feet. Not cold. Not warm. No different from the shade of any other tree in Eden.

She raised her hand.

Adam drew breath.

Eve stopped with the width of a fingernail between her fingers and the fruit.

“I have not touched it.”

“I see.”

“Where does the danger begin?”

“When it is eaten.”

“Touching it?”

“The Decree does not say.”

“Plucked?”

“It does not say.”

“Smelled?”

“It does not say.”

“Questioned?”

Adam remained silent.

Eve lowered her hand.

She walked around the trunk. The gray bark bore lines that divided and met again, but none completed a shape. Behind the tree, one root rose briefly above the earth before sinking back beneath it. Between two roots lay a black stone, smaller than the one Lilith had once left behind, but the same color.

Eve did not pick up that stone.

She found two pale stones at the water’s edge and set them at the border of the tree’s shadow, one handspan apart.

“What is the mark?”

“Where I stop.”

“Because of the prohibition?”

“Because I do not yet know.”

Adam looked at the two stones.

“Is there a difference?”

“Yes.”

Eve pointed to the stone nearer Adam.

“If I stop only because you are afraid, this step will always have to wait upon your fear.”

She pointed to the other stone.

“If I step forward merely to defy the Decree, the step will no longer belong to what I see.”

She placed her hand upon the ground between the two stones.

“I stop here because this part has no answer yet.”

Adam looked at his hands.

Long ago, he had set stones to show Lilith the way back.

Now Eve set stones to mark the place she had chosen not to cross.

“May I remain with you?”

Eve looked at the open space beside her.

“Yes.”

Adam sat down.

He did not place himself between her and the tree.

He did not stand behind her.

He sat on the same side as the question.

For a long while, there was only the sound of water behind them.

Eve looked at the nearest fruit.

“When I do not know. what is being protected—my life, or only the prohibition?”

Adam did not answer in haste.

“I want it to be your life.”

“What you want is not an answer.”

“No.”

“Then who knows?”

Adam looked toward the shapeless brightness above the two crowns.

“He who gave the Decree.”

Eve waited.

No voice passed through the leaves.

✦

Within the Archive, a new line was created beneath the observation record.

Not a warning.

Not a violation.

Not a request for sanction.

EVE: APPROACHED THE DECLARED LIMIT.

EVE: MADE NO CONTACT WITH THE FRUIT.

EVE: ESTABLISHED HER OWN STOPPING POINT.

Gabriel read the final line twice.

“The system has no corresponding classification.”

“Then preserve the description as it stands.”

“Every act near the central region must bear a status.”

“It already has a status.”

“What is the status called?”

Healiangel looked at the tablet.

The curve within the hollow beneath his wing ceased to move.

It did not disappear.

It merely stopped in an unfinished shape.

“Undecided.”

Gabriel looked at him.

“That is not a state Heaven permits to endure.”

“But it is what occurred.”

Before Gabriel could answer, a secondary tablet lit along the observation channel.

The characters appeared slowly, not wholly following the syntax of Heaven.

WHEN I DO NOT KNOW, WHAT IS BEING PROTECTED—MY LIFE, OR THE PROHIBITION?

Gabriel raised his staff.

Michael caught his wrist.

Not forcefully.

Only enough to halt the staff before it reached the words.

“Do not erase it.”

“It is not a Decree.”

“No one said it was.”

“It does not belong to the structure of the record.”

“It now belongs to the observation.”

“Who inscribed it?”

Healiangel looked down toward Eden.

Eve still sat beside Adam at the edge of the tree’s shadow. Her lips had closed. No path of reply ran from the Archive down to her.

“Her question was recorded.” “Nothing more.”

Gabriel looked at the words.

“The system has no answer.”

Michael released his wrist.

“Record what occurred.”

No one added an explanation.

No one turned the question into a violation.

No one answered in her place.

At the heart of Eden, the two crowns remained still.

A leaf came free from the Tree of Knowledge.

No wind touched the crown.

No light altered its rhythm.

No one knew why the stem released at that moment.

The leaf turned once and came to rest upon the earth between the two stones Eve had placed—exactly where she had chosen to stop.

Eve looked at it.

Adam looked as well.

Neither of them called it an answer.
